items.question: How many intervals does a smallest subcover use?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Start at 0 and reach as far as you can each time.

byKey.all: You kept every interval. Two of them add nothing.
byKey.two: No two intervals cover $[0, 1]$: the one holding 0 stops at 0.4, and none from there reaches 1.

explain.text: Only $(-0.1, 0.4)$ holds 0. From 0.4 the furthest reach is $(0.3, 0.7)$, and from 0.7 it is $(0.6, 1.2)$. So 3 intervals, and no two suffice.

items.prose: Let $f(x) = x^2$ on the compact set $[-1, 2]$.
items.question: What is $f([-1, 2])$?

options.why: You used only the ends. $f(0) = 0$ is the minimum, inside the interval.
A continuous image of a compact set is compact, hence closed: 0 and 4 are attained.

feedback.correct: Right. Compact, so the ends are attained.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the minimum and maximum on $[-1, 2]$.

explain.text: On $[-1, 2]$, $x^2$ has minimum 0 at 0 and maximum 4 at 2. The image $[0, 4]$ is compact, as the theorem promises.

items.question: Which are complete? Select all that apply.

options.why: Truncations of $\sqrt2$ are Cauchy with no rational limit.
$\tfrac1n$ is Cauchy with its limit 0 missing.

feedback.generic: Not quite. In $\mathbb{R}$, complete means closed.

explain.text: Inside the complete $\mathbb{R}$, complete subsets are closed ones: $\mathbb{R}$, $[0, 1]$ and $\mathbb{Z}$. In $\mathbb{Z}$ a Cauchy sequence is eventually constant.

items.question: Which hypothesis of the contraction mapping theorem fails, beyond completeness?

options.why: $(0, 1)$ is incomplete, but that is not the only failure: $T$ also leaves the space.

explain.text: For $x \in (0, 1)$, $T(x) = \tfrac x3 + 1 \in (1, \tfrac43)$, outside $X$. So $T$ is not a map from $X$ to itself, and the theorem says nothing.

items.question: What is the smallest $n$ whose a priori bound is below 0.001?

byKey.eleven: 11 drops the factor $\tfrac{1}{1 - q}$, which bounds one step only. With it, $4 \times 0.5^{11} \approx 0.00195$ is still above 0.001.

explain.text: The bound is $\tfrac{0.5^n}{0.5} \times 2 = 4 \times 0.5^n$. It is $0.00195$ at $n = 11$ and $0.00098$ at $n = 12$, so 12 steps.

items.prose: With the ramps $f_n$ of l11 and $d_1(f_n, f_m) = |\tfrac{1}{2n} - \tfrac{1}{2m}|$.
items.question: What is $d_1(f_5, f_{10})$?

byKey.sup: 0.5 is the sup distance. $d_1$ measures area.

explain.text: $d_1(f_5, f_{10}) = \tfrac{1}{10} - \tfrac{1}{20} = 0.05$. The ramps are Cauchy in $d_1$ with a discontinuous limit, so $(C[0, 1], d_1)$ is not complete.
